extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their agents seeking to accelerate patent examination in ASEAN using the ASPEC programmes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and qualifying ASPEC (including ASPEC AIM and PCT‑ASPEC) requests to accelerate patent examination among participating ASEAN IP Offices, including eligibility, required documents, procedures, scope, and programme limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-track patenting across 9 ASEAN IP Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast-track patenting process in any 9 ASEAN IP Office
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC is a regional patent work‑sharing programme among 9 participating ASEAN Member States (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Viet Nam) that allows applicants to use search and examination (S&E) reports of one participating IP Office to accelerate patenting in another participating IP Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: One common form with no additional fee
rubrics_metrics.description: One common form with no additional fee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC uses a single ASPEC Request Form; there is no additional fee for filing an ASPEC request. Note: submission of the ASPEC Request Form is mandatory for the IP Offices of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR., Malaysia, Philippines, and Thailand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate in English resulting in potential cost saving for translation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC requests can be made in English which may reduce translation costs. ASPEC requests can also be filed electronically via the ASEAN IP Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM — Industry 4.0 prioritisation and 6‑month first office action
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC AIM: a committed turnaround time of 6 months to receive the first office action if an ASPEC request is made for Industry 4.0 patent applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC AIM prioritises Industry 4.0 patent applications for first office actions to be issued within 6 months. Applicants should refer to the applicable IPCs list to determine whether an invention is related to Industry 4.0.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT‑ASPEC — rely on PCT reports from ASEAN ISA/IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT‑ASPEC: additional choice of relying on Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) reports issued from an ASEAN International Searching Authority/International Preliminary Examining Authority (ISA/IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under PCT‑ASPEC, applicants may rely on PCT written opinions or international preliminary examination reports issued by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA (currently Singapore and the Philippines). Supplementary international search reports are not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and capacity limits / pilot periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Programme duration, pilot periods and annual application capacity vary by stream
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ASPEC programme has been in operation since 2009. The page lists acceptance and pilot extension dates and annual capacities (table entries reference acceptance of written opinions for ASPEC requests from 15 June 2021, pilot extensions to 26 August 2025, and annual application capacities noted in the programme comparison table). Applicants should consult the programme notices/brochures for up‑to‑date capacity and pilot status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of invention eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of Invention: All types (ASPEC) / Inventions related to Industry 4.0 (ASPEC AIM) / All types (PCT‑ASPEC)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC accepts all types of inventions; ASPEC AIM is limited to inventions related to Industry 4.0 (see the Appendix/List of Qualifying IPCs). PCT‑ASPEC similarly covers all types where PCT reports are available from an ASEAN ISA/IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying criteria — basic eligibility for ASPEC requests
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC request can be filed at any participating IP Office if you have (i) filed a corresponding patent application for the same invention in any other participating IP Office and (ii) Written opinion or final examination report issued by one of the participating IP Offices with at least one allowable claim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The participating IP Office that issued the examination report is the “first IP Office”. The participating IP Office where the ASPEC Request Form is filed is the “second IP Office”. Under PCT‑ASPEC, the ASEAN ISA/IPEA that issued the international preliminary examination report/written opinion is the first IP Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — acceptable S&E results
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable to written opinion or final examination report established by participating IP Offices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC relies on national written opinions or final examination reports issued by participating IP Offices. If IPOS is the first IP Office, the ASPEC result may be based on: a request for a search report (Patent Form 10); a request for a S&E report (Patent Form 11); or a request for an examination report (Patent Form 12). PCT‑ASPEC applies to PCT reports from ASEAN ISA/IPEA but excludes supplementary international search reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional fee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no extra fee charged specifically for making an ASPEC request (beyond normal national filing/examination fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period to file ASPEC request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time before final decision of grant or refusal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC requests must be filed at the second IP Office any time prior to the final decision to grant or refuse the application in that Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and documentation required — ASPEC (national written opinion/final exam report)
rubrics_metrics.description: File completed ASPEC Request Form; copy of the written opinion or final examination report; copy of claims referred to with at least one allowable claim; and email PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg and the second IP Office ASPEC focal point with application details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents to file in the second IP Office: the completed ASPEC Request Form (where applicable), copy of the written opinion or final examination report, and copy of the claims showing at least one allowable claim. Additionally, email PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg and the second IP Office ASPEC focal point with: application number from the first IP Office; desired second IP Office and application number in the second IP Office; date of request; and applicant name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and documentation required — ASPEC AIM (Industry 4.0 prioritisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Same core documents as ASPEC, with indication that it is an ASPEC AIM request and emailing the ASPEC AIM focal point
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the completed ASPEC Request Form (indicate ASPEC AIM in the form or a cover letter), copy of the written opinion or final examination report, and copy of the claims with at least one allowable claim. Email PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg and the second IP Office ASPEC AIM focal point with the application number from the first IP Office, desired second IP Office and application number in the second IP Office, date of request, and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and documentation required — PCT‑ASPEC
rubrics_metrics.description: File completed ASPEC Request Form (indicate PCT‑ASPEC), copy of written opinion or IPE report from an ASEAN ISA/IPEA, copy of claims with at least one allowable claim, and email PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg and PCT‑ASPEC focal point with PCT and national application details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on a PCT report, submit the international preliminary examination report/written opinion established by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA; provide the International Search Report where applicable. Email PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg and the second IP Office PCT‑ASPEC focal point with the PCT application number, desired second IP Office and application number in the second IP Office, date of request, and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of written opinion (post‑15 June 2021) and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For ASPEC requests made on or after 15 June 2021, written opinion is an acceptable S&E result for all participating AMS IP Offices except the IP Office of Thailand
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one written opinion from participating AMS IP Offices may be used to support an ASPEC request. Applicants relying on written opinions should verify whether the first IP Office's S&E result is a written opinion or a final examination report and whether the chosen second IP Office accepts written opinions for ASPEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory ASPEC Request Form submission to certain IP Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: It is mandatory to submit an ASPEC request form to the IP Offices of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR., Malaysia, Philippines, and Thailand
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the filing requirements of the particular second IP Office: some offices require the physical ASPEC Request Form to be submitted; others may accept the necessary documents through electronic channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASEAN ISA/IPEA identity note
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, ASEAN ISA/IPEA refers to the IP Offices of Singapore and the Philippines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using PCT‑ASPEC, ensure the PCT reports relied on were issued by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA (currently Singapore or the Philippines) to qualify under PCT‑ASPEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC requests can be made electronically through the ASEAN IP Portal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may use the ASEAN IP Portal to submit ASPEC requests electronically; follow portal instructions and ensure all required documents are uploaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and referral documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference materials and contacts are provided (ASPEC brochure, Notice and Procedures, IPC list, ASPEC Request Form, Claims Correspondence Table, and PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the ASPEC brochure and Notice and Procedures PDFs, the Appendix of qualifying IPCs for ASPEC AIM, and use the official ASPEC Request Form and Claims Correspondence Table. For queries, contact PT_acceleration@ipos.gov.sg.
